# Implementation Plan: Fix crews liveness-notifications crash-sweep lock contention

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-24. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/crews-liveness-notifications-lock-contention-hook-errored/plan.md`.*

## Overview

The crews lead-side member-crash sweep holds the per-crew `liveness-notifications.json.lock` across an O(N-members) crew scan (`listNames` + per-member `readManifest` + `getMemberHealth`, which calls Windows CIM `describeProcess` per live-PID launcher). On a large crew (the live `ralph-pipeline` crew has **555 member directories**) the lock is held far longer than the default 2000 ms acquire budget, so a second lead-side sweeper running in a different process times out: `LockTimeoutError: timed out after 2000ms acquiring …/liveness-notifications.json.lock`. The error already fails soft (all four sweep call sites try/catch + `appendLog('member-crash-sweep-failed …')`), so **no tool is denied** — but it produces recurring log noise (17+ occurrences in one session) and can delay (never lose) a real member-crash notification.

The fix restructures `sweepMemberCrashNotifications` so the expensive read-only crew scan runs **outside** the latch lock, taking the lock only briefly to read the latch, dedupe each candidate, append the `member-crashed` envelope, and write the latch. This collapses the lock-hold window from `O(N members × CIM)` to `O(notify-count × small file write)`, eliminating the contention regardless of crew size while preserving every existing correctness invariant (persist-after-append, no-double-notify, corrupt-latch recovery, latch-write-fail tolerance). The mandatory fail-soft invariant — a sweep/lock error must never deny a member-facing tool — is preserved and hardened with an explicit regression test.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

All paths are under `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/` (crews plugin, v3.23.2; JavaScript-only, synchronous Node hooks; no package build/typecheck — validate with `node tests/run.js` + `node --check`).

- **The sweep, fully under the lock today:** `sweepMemberCrashNotifications` (`hooks/member-crash-notifications.js:238`) wraps the entire body in `withStateFileLock(getLatchPath(crew, cwd), cwd, () => { … })` at `:262-350`. Inside the lock it runs `readLatch`, then `listNames(crew, cwd)`, then a per-member loop of `readManifest` + the six skip guards + `getMemberHealth` + `buildDeadSignature` + `appendSystemMailbox` + `setLatchSignature`, then `writeJsonAtomicWithRetry(latch)` at `:336-349`.
- **The throttle is checked before the lock** (`:249-254`): `shouldThrottleTurnBoundarySweep` (`:129-141`) / `turnStampPath` (`:116-119`) / `getCrashSweepThrottleMs` (`:106-114`) — a lock-free per-lead stamp-file mtime gate, used only when the caller passes `throttle: true`.
- **Scan cost:** `listNames` returns members + leads + tasks (`hooks/actors.js:1606-1615`) — it includes dead member dirs. `getMemberHealth` (`hooks/health.js`) calls `resolvePidAlive` (`hooks/health.js:101-176`) which, for a live-PID launcher on win32, performs a CIM `describeProcess` + `verifyLauncherRecycleSafety` — the per-member expensive step. There is a cheap ESRCH pre-check, but any member with a live-but-unverifiable launcher PID triggers a CIM query.
- **Lock primitive:** `withStateFileLock(file, cwd, fn, timeoutMs)` (`hooks/locks.js:223-231`) calls `acquireLock(file + '.lock', timeoutMs || DEFAULT_MAILBOX_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS)`; the default is `2000` ms (`hooks/locks.js:24`). The sweep passes no timeout, so it uses 2000 ms. `acquireLock` already applies the dead-holder steal (`isDeadLocalHolderLock` / `lockCanBeStolen` / `stealStaleLock`, `hooks/locks.js:88-193`), but that only steals from a **dead** holder — irrelevant here because the contending holder is a live sibling sweeper.
- **Second latch-lock site:** `resetMemberCrashNotificationLatch` (`hooks/member-crash-notifications.js:357-377`) also takes the latch lock via `withStateFileLock`, but only on the `/clear-member` path (`hooks/commands/clear-member.js`) and only does a single-row clear — not a hot path; out of scope for the contention fix but must keep working.
- **Two independent throttles (the multi-process collision):**
  - Hook backstop (pre-tool-use/stop/session-start) → file-stamp throttle `shouldThrottleTurnBoundarySweep` (`member-crash-notifications.js:83-141`).
  - Listener-loop heartbeat-tick (D-001) → in-process closure `lastCrashSweepAt` (`lib/listener-loop.js:408-440`, helpers ~339-424).
  These are separate processes with separate throttle state, so both can fire in the same ~60 s window and collide on the long-held lock.
- **Four sweep call sites, all already fail-soft (lead-only, try/catch + appendLog):** `hooks/pre-tool-use.js:475-485` (`throttle: true`), `hooks/stop.js:912-922`, `hooks/session-start.js:509-517`, `lib/listener-loop.js:418-431`. None calls `block()` on a sweep error.
- **Tests:** `tests/member-crash-notifications.test.js` (skip guards, latch persistence, throttle, EPERM-tolerant latch write — injects a `getMemberHealth`/`now`/`throttleMs` seam), `tests/member-crash-backstop-reset.test.js` (clear-member latch reset + call-site source-grep). Runner: `tests/run.js` (per-file worker; single file via positional arg; serial denylist via `--serial-denylist`; scrubs `CREWS_*` + agent-session env per worker). Version stamps: `scripts/bump-version.js` (6 stamps + `tests/version.test.js`).

### Technical Constraints

- **The latch lock only needs to serialize the dedupe state in `liveness-notifications.json`** — it never protected member manifests or health state. So the expensive crew scan can safely run outside it (independently confirmed by both the Copilot reviewer and the architect pass).
- **Persist-after-append is load-bearing** (`member-crash-notifications.js:307-349`): the `appendSystemMailbox` must succeed before the latch signature is set/written. On latch-write failure a duplicate notification next sweep is acceptable; a lost notification is not. The brief-lock phase must keep this exact ordering.
- **No-double-notify must survive** concurrent sweeps: two sweeps that each independently compute the same candidate must not both append. With the brief lock, the second sweep's `readLatchSignature === signature` dedupe check (`:304-305`) sees the first's latch write and skips — so serialization at dedupe time preserves the guarantee.
- **The `appended` return value is load-bearing for the listener** (`lib/listener-loop.js:432`): `sweepResult.appended > 0` triggers an in-tick `deliver('crash-sweep')`. The restructured function must keep returning `{ appended, notified }` (and the throttle short-circuit `{ appended: 0, notified: [], throttled: true }`).
- **Do NOT raise the 2000 ms timeout** (e.g. to 30 s). With the scan moved out of the lock, the lock is held for milliseconds and 2000 ms is more than sufficient. Raising the timeout would instead make the pre-tool-use hot path BLOCK for up to 30 s waiting on a lock — strictly worse than the current fail-soft skip.
- **`appendSystemMailbox` takes its own mailbox lock.** It is already invoked under the latch lock today (latch-lock → mailbox-lock nesting already exists at `:311-325`), so keeping it under the brief latch lock does not introduce a new lock-ordering relationship.
- **Cross-engine:** the sweep is engine-agnostic; it runs under claude/copilot/codex leads. The live incident is a copilot lead. No engine-specific code changes; tests should not assume an engine.

## Approach

### Architecture

Split `sweepMemberCrashNotifications` into two phases with a clear boundary:

**Phase A — unlocked scan (no latch lock held).** Keep the existing top-of-function throttle short-circuit. Then perform the crew scan exactly as today (`listNames` → per-member `readManifest` + skip guards 1-5 + `getMemberHealth` + skip guard 6 + `resolveOwnership` + `buildDeadSignature`), but instead of appending inside the loop, **collect a `candidates` array** of `{ name, signature, health, detectedAt, message, payload }`. The orphan-skip `appendLog` stays in this phase (it is a pure log). No latch read, no lock.

**Phase B — brief locked dedupe + re-validate + append + write.** Acquire the latch lock via `withStateFileLock(getLatchPath(...))`. Inside: `readLatch` (keep the corrupt-latch try/catch → fresh-latch fallback and `appendLog`); for each candidate: (i) **re-read the candidate's manifest and re-check the cheap manifest-based skip guards** (#1 role==member, #2 not intentionally-stopped, #3 not recoverable, #5 ownership) — this closes the TOCTOU where `clear-member` / resume / `/stop-member` flipped `shutdownRequested`/`terminationKind`/`terminatedAt`/`listenerState` between the unlocked scan and the locked append; skip the candidate if any guard now fails. Do NOT re-run `getMemberHealth` here (that would reintroduce per-candidate CIM under the lock — the health-dead snapshot from the scan is acceptable). (ii) `readLatchSignature(latch, leadName, name)` — if it equals the candidate signature, skip. (iii) otherwise `appendSystemMailbox(...)` (persist-after-append), then `setLatchSignature(...)` and mark `latchDirty`. After the loop, if `latchDirty`, `writeJsonAtomicWithRetry(getLatchPath(...), latch)` with the existing AC4 transient-error handling. Return `{ appended, notified }`.

This is behavior-preserving except for the lock-hold window. The candidate set is computed from a health snapshot taken just before the lock; the per-candidate manifest re-validation under the lock keeps the intentionally-stopped/cleared/recoverable guards authoritative at append time, and the dedupe re-check is the authority that prevents double-notify. Re-reading one manifest per candidate is cheap (a single `readManifest`, no CIM) and bounded by the notify-count, not the crew size.

### Implementation Strategy

1. **US-001 (root fix):** Refactor `sweepMemberCrashNotifications` into Phase A (unlocked scan → `candidates[]`) + Phase B (brief locked per-candidate re-validation + dedupe + append + latch write). Preserve the return contract, throttle short-circuit, persist-after-append ordering, corrupt-latch fallback, and AC4 latch-write-fail handling. Add tests: (a) a **fail-soft** regression — a forced `LockTimeoutError` (or any throw) from the sweep does not throw out of `pre-tool-use.js` / does not deny the triggering tool (fixture satisfies the other PreToolUse gates, incl. an armed listener); (b) a **lock-window** assertion via an injected recording lock seam (or monkeypatch-before-require) proving `listNames`/`getMemberHealth` run before the latch lock is acquired; (c) the **re-validation TOCTOU** case (stop/recoverable marker flipped between scan and append → zero appends). Keep `member-crash-notifications.test.js` + `member-crash-backstop-reset.test.js` + `tests/integration/member-crash-listener-delivery.test.js` green.
2. **US-002 (optional, deferrable — secondary):** Coordinate the two sweepers so the (now lock-free but still O(N) CPU) crew scan does not run redundantly twice per window. Make the listener-loop D-001 sweep consult the same shared per-lead file-stamp debounce that the hook backstop uses (`shouldThrottleTurnBoundarySweep`), so at most one sweep performs the full scan per crew/lead per window. This is a CPU/efficiency optimization, NOT required to fix the reported LockTimeoutError (US-001 alone removes the contention). It carries a small, acceptable risk of slightly delaying crash detection (the outbox + listener re-arm still surface the data). Ship only if low-risk; otherwise defer.

   > **US-002 does NOT gate the bugfix.** The reported `LockTimeoutError` is fully resolved by US-001 alone. None of the US-001 acceptance criteria depend on US-002, and ship-readiness for the fix is determined by US-001 (+ US-003 release ceremony) only. US-002 may be dropped or split into a follow-up task without affecting the fix.
3. **US-003 (release ceremony):** Standard crews version bump + changelog + AGENTS.md table (see Files to Create/Modify). Depends on US-001 (and US-002 if shipped). **Must serialize after any in-flight crews impl** (e.g. impl-rmoutbox) because it touches the shared version stamps / CHANGELOG / AGENTS.md table.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Restructure `sweepMemberCrashNotifications` to move the read-only crew scan outside the latch lock (US-001).
- Preserve all six skip guards, persist-after-append ordering, no-double-notify dedupe, corrupt-latch fallback, AC4 latch-write-fail handling, throttle short-circuit, and the `{ appended, notified }` return contract.
- Add **required** per-candidate manifest re-validation under the brief lock (re-check guards #1/#2/#3/#5 before append) to close the scan→append TOCTOU.
- Harden the fail-soft invariant with an explicit hook-level regression test; add a lock-window assertion test.
- (Optional) Unify the two sweepers' throttle to avoid redundant full scans (US-002).
- Crews version bump + changelog + AGENTS.md table (US-003).

### Out of Scope
- Raising the 2000 ms lock timeout (explicitly rejected — would block the hot path).
- Changing the dead-holder steal helper in `hooks/locks.js` (already active; not the fix for live contention).
- Reducing the crew size / pruning the 555-member roster (separate operational concern).
- Changing `getMemberHealth` / `resolvePidAlive` / CIM behavior.
- `resetMemberCrashNotificationLatch` behavior (clear-member path) beyond keeping it working.
- Any change to the four sweep call sites' fail-soft try/catch wrappers (they stay; the test asserts they stay).

## Risk Areas

- **Stale candidate set between unlocked scan and locked append (TOCTOU).** The scan→append window grows with this refactor (Phase A computes ALL candidates before Phase B appends any, so an early candidate's gap is now ~the rest of the scan, not ~0). Mitigated by the **required** per-candidate manifest re-validation under the brief lock (re-check guards #1/#2/#3/#5 before append) — this preserves the intentionally-stopped/cleared/recoverable guards' intent. The in-lock dedupe re-check remains the no-double-notify authority. (Flagged by Copilot + Codex; made required.)
- **Refactor regressions in the six skip guards or persist-after-append ordering.** Mitigated by keeping the guard logic byte-identical (only relocating where the append happens) and by the existing unit tests + new coverage.
- **Concurrency test flakiness on Windows** (the runner already serial-denylists race-sensitive files). New contention test should use deterministic injected seams (held lock / wrapped `withStateFileLock`) rather than real timing races, and be added to the serial denylist if it spawns real processes.
- **US-002 throttle unification could mask a real crash window** if the shared stamp suppresses a needed sweep. Mitigated by treating US-002 as optional/deferrable and by the fact that the outbox + listener re-arm independently surface crash data.
- **Split-export / public-surface drift.** Keep the module's `module.exports` + `_internal` seam shapes stable (tests pin them). The lock-window test's injectable lock is an additive optional `args.withStateFileLock` parameter (or a recording stub installed via monkeypatch-before-require) — it does not change the existing export surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `sweepMemberCrashNotifications` performs `listNames` + per-member `readManifest` + `getMemberHealth` + skip guards + `buildDeadSignature` **without holding** the `liveness-notifications.json` latch lock; the latch lock is acquired only for the dedupe-read + per-candidate `appendSystemMailbox` + `setLatchSignature` + final `writeJsonAtomicWithRetry`.
- [ ] Persist-after-append ordering is preserved (latch signature is set/written only after `appendSystemMailbox` succeeds for that candidate).
- [ ] No-double-notify is preserved: a test with two sweeps over the same dead member (second sees the first's latch row) appends exactly once.
- [ ] The return value remains `{ appended, notified }` and the throttle short-circuit remains `{ appended: 0, notified: [], throttled: true }`; `lib/listener-loop.js`'s `appended > 0` deliver path still fires.
- [ ] Corrupt-latch fallback and AC4 latch-write-fail handling are unchanged (existing tests stay green).
- [ ] **Fail-soft invariant**: a forced sweep error (e.g. `LockTimeoutError`) does NOT throw out of `pre-tool-use.js` and does NOT deny the triggering tool — asserted by a new regression test. **The fixture MUST satisfy the other PreToolUse gates** (lead role, an armed listener / `listenerState: 'armed'`, no pending review-required mail, a non-`.crews`-write tool) so the test proves the sweep-error path is fail-soft, NOT that the tool was coincidentally allowed/blocked for an unrelated reason (e.g. the arm-first gate). Assert the decision is `allow`/no-deny while the injected sweep throws.
- [ ] **Candidate re-validation under the brief lock (closes the scan→append TOCTOU)**: before `appendSystemMailbox` for each candidate, the sweep re-reads the candidate's manifest under the brief latch lock and re-checks the cheap manifest-based skip guards (#1 role, #2 intentionally-stopped, #3 recoverable, #5 ownership); a candidate that was `/stop-member`/`/clear-member`/resumed between the unlocked scan and the locked append is skipped (no false `member-crashed`). `getMemberHealth` is NOT re-run under the lock. A test seeds a candidate, flips `shutdownRequested`/`terminationKind` (or `listenerState: 'recoverable'`) between scan and append, and asserts zero appends.
- [ ] **Lock-window invariant (observably verifiable, specified mechanism)**: a new test proves the crew scan does NOT run under the latch lock. The test MUST use a deterministic call-order assertion, NOT a timing/duration claim and NOT a real held-lock 2 s timeout. Use ONE of these mechanisms (the impl picks; the AC requires the chosen mechanism be observable):
  - **(preferred) Injectable lock seam**: add an optional `args.withStateFileLock` (or equivalent `_internal`-exposed lock function) to `sweepMemberCrashNotifications`, defaulting to the real `require('./locks').withStateFileLock`. This is additive (a new optional arg; `module.exports`/`_internal` shapes are otherwise unchanged). The test injects a recording wrapper and asserts every `listNames`/`getMemberHealth` call is recorded BEFORE the first latch-lock acquisition.
  - **(alternative) Monkeypatch-before-require**: because the module destructures `withStateFileLock` (`hooks/member-crash-notifications.js:59`) and `getMemberHealth` (`:75`) at load, the test must bust the `require` cache, install recording stubs on `../hooks/locks` and `../hooks/health`, then `require` the module fresh, and assert the scan calls precede the lock acquisition.
  A real external-held-lock fixture is explicitly discouraged (it depends on the 2000 ms `LockTimeoutError` and is Windows-flaky); if used at all it must be in the serial denylist.
- [ ] `tests/member-crash-notifications.test.js` and `tests/member-crash-backstop-reset.test.js` pass unchanged in intent (only additive cases).
- [ ] Full crews suite passes: `node ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/tests/run.js` (with `CREWS_*` + agent-session env scrubbed). `node --check` passes on every touched JS file.
- [ ] (US-003) Version bumped via `scripts/bump-version.js`; `tests/version.test.js` green; `CHANGELOG.md` entry prepended; codexu `AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table updated in the codexu pointer-bump commit.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

- **US-001** — Restructure `sweepMemberCrashNotifications` (scan outside lock; brief lock for dedupe/append/write) + fail-soft + lock-window regression tests. (root fix; the reported bug is resolved by this story alone.)
- **US-002** — (optional/deferrable) Unify the listener-loop + hook-backstop sweep throttles on a shared per-lead debounce to avoid redundant full crew scans. Depends on US-001. **If shipped, requires a listener-delivery test**: `lib/listener-loop.js:424,432` only calls `deliver('crash-sweep')` when its own sweep returns `appended > 0`; a shared stamp could make the listener skip its scan after a hook-side sweep already touched the stamp, so the test must prove the listener still wakes/drains a crash notice the hook backstop appended (the queued envelope is delivered on the listener's next `fs.watch` wake — assert that path).
- **US-003** — Crews release ceremony (version bump, changelog). Depends on US-001 (+US-002 if shipped). Must serialize after any in-flight crews impl. **Two-commit submodule flow**: the impl member commits the crews changes INSIDE `ai-developer-toolkit/` (the 6 version stamps via `scripts/bump-version.js`, `tests/version.test.js`, prepended `CHANGELOG.md`) on its topic branch — it must NOT leave a dirty submodule. The codexu parent-pointer bump and the codexu root `AGENTS.md` active-plugin-versions table update are the **lead's** responsibility after merging the submodule branch (per codexu AGENTS.md), in the same commit that records the new `ai-developer-toolkit` SHA.

## Suggested Decomposition

All stories touch the **same plugin** (`ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews`) and US-003 rewrites the shared version stamps / `CHANGELOG.md` / `AGENTS.md` table. They cannot run in parallel — same-plugin parallel produces conflicting version-file and changelog writes. Single serial cluster.

## Open Questions

- **Should US-002 (throttle unification) ship in this batch or be deferred?** Recommendation: ship US-001 + US-003 first (they fix the reported bug); treat US-002 as a follow-up unless the redundant lock-free scans show measurable CPU cost. The impl can decide based on review.
- **Target crews version for US-003:** likely a patch bump from the version current at impl time (3.23.2 today, but impl-rmoutbox may bump it first — the impl must rebase onto the latest crews main and bump from there). Left to the impl/lead at ship time.
- **Re-validation depth under the brief lock:** the plan requires re-reading the candidate manifest and re-checking the cheap manifest-based guards (#1/#2/#3/#5) before append, but deliberately does NOT re-run `getMemberHealth` (#4/#6) under the lock (that would reintroduce per-candidate CIM). Open question for impl: is manifest-only re-validation sufficient, or is there a realistic case where health flips from dead→alive in the scan→append window that warrants a cheap (non-CIM) liveness re-check? Default: manifest-only (a dead→alive flip in a sub-second window is a benign at-worst-duplicate, caught by dedupe next sweep).
